Can local AI recover document headings?

Headings tell a search system what a passage is for: an executive summary may answer a user’s question; an acronyms list may not. We tested local tools on WFP evaluation reports to see whether they preserve both headings and their hierarchy.

Results at a glance

34 configurations · 4 WFP reports · 32 audited pages · 77 reference headings · Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB

  • Highest score: Qwen3.6-27B with visual memory gets 65/77 heading-level pairs right; 54 min 2 sec for 32 pages. It receives extra PDF text, tags and document context.
  • Image-only alternative: Chandra OCR 2 gets 53/77 right in 14 min 46 sec. OvisOCR3 gets 36/77 right in 6 min 58 sec.
  • OUR METHOD: small trained CPU classifiers get 34/77 right with two extra headings. Fast, but the missing headings make this configuration unsuitable when coverage matters.

Score = correct title, page and level. F0.5 favors precision; recall shows what is missing. References are assistant annotations without independent review.

How the experiment works

  1. Annotate: identify heading text, page and level on the same 32 pages. Main chapters and annexes are H1. Pages · Reference labels.
  2. Extract: run each local configuration without reference labels. CPU parsers process the complete PDFs; later OCR models process page images. Some Qwen runs also receive native text, tags and document context. These are different input conditions.
  3. Match and score: match titles one-to-one on the same page, using normalized similarity ≥90%. Award joint credit only when the level also matches. Scorer.
  4. Measure: record processing time and, where applicable, retained prose. Run large models one at a time. No per-report heading corrections are applied.

Three kinds of technique

Approach What happens Examples
PDF parser Read PDF text or use OCR; infer heading styles and hierarchy. Docling, PyMuPDF4LLM, MinerU basic
Local vision model Read page images; generate text and structure. Some configurations add text or document context. Chandra, Qwen, MiniCPM, Xiaomi, Paddle
OUR METHOD Use assistant-labeled reports to train small Extra Trees classifiers for line grouping, heading levels and neighboring-heading relationships. No LLM runs at inference. Original, calibrated and confidence-filtered variants

A row’s i opens only that configuration’s flow and settings. Expand its predictions to inspect misses and wrong levels. Runnable repository · Reproduction guide.

What is shared across the runs?

We preserve each pipeline’s output without WFP-specific level repairs. Different inputs are explicit: native-text parsers, image-only OCR, and Qwen with additional document context. Page numbers count from the cover. Predictions and references use the same scorer in the table and dialogs.

OUR METHOD uses Extra Trees: classifiers that combine randomized decision trees. Its variants learn from assistant annotations on separate reports. Each dialog identifies the fitted components and the validation choices for that variant; it links the full training record.

Primary metric: heading-and-level F0.5

A correct prediction must match title, page and exact level. Let C be correct predictions, P all predictions and G reference headings. Counts are pooled across the four reports before scoring.

Measure Formula Meaning
Joint F0.5 1.25C / (P + 0.25G) Primary score; weights precision more than recall.
Joint precision C / P How much of the output is correct, including level?
Joint recall C / G How much of the reference was recovered correctly?
Joint F1 2C / (P + G) Equal emphasis on precision and recall.

Wrong level = both a false positive and a false negative. An invented heading is a false positive; a missed heading is a false negative. Unknown levels receive no joint credit. No predictions scores zero. Heading-only detection ignores level mistakes and is available as a diagnostic; there is no separate PASS/FAIL gate.

Example: 10 reference headings, 12 predictions and 9 correct heading-level pairs give precision 75%, recall 90%, and F0.5 77.6%. Recovering every title is not enough if the levels are wrong.

Selection history: OUR METHOD’s confidence filter was selected on separate validation reports using joint F0.5 with a heading-only precision constraint. The published training procedure has not been changed retrospectively. Its full selection rule, thresholds and provenance are in the method modal and experiment record.

Model names and technical terms

Models and terms explained

Qwen3.6-27B
A pretrained model used here to read page images together with text context; 27B identifies its model size.
MLX
Apple’s machine-learning framework used here to run models locally on Apple Silicon. It is the execution software, not the heading model.
4-bit / 8-bit weights
Reduced-precision representations of a model’s learned numbers, used to lower memory requirements. The number describes storage precision, not heading depth or model accuracy.
4-bit
Quantized model weights use reduced numerical precision to lower memory requirements. This does not specify heading depth or guarantee a speedup.
Chandra OCR 2
A document image-reading model that produces structured text; this benchmark reads HTML heading tags from its output.
bf16
A 16-bit floating-point number format used for model weights and calculations. It is a numerical format, not a particular model or training technique.
Extra Trees
A classifier that averages predictions from many randomized decision trees. A tree makes a sequence of decisions about input measurements. This benchmark uses scikit-learn’s ExtraTreesClassifier, with 200 trees per component.
Features
The numeric measurements supplied to a classifier—for example font size, boldness, line spacing or whether a title occurs in the table of contents. They are calculated from the PDF, not supplied reference answers.
Validation reports
Reports kept separate from model fitting and used to choose between designs or decision settings. The later inspected test reports are now regression checks: they can expose a failure but no longer provide a fresh independent evaluation.
Viterbi decoding
An algorithm for choosing the highest-scoring sequence of heading levels. Here it combines each heading’s own scores with scores for the relationship to the preceding heading. It does not train or add another model.
model provenance page
Complete training lineage, report list, model identities and reproduction command.
training run record
Original structure-v2 training output: counts, versions, selection and saved model hashes.
training program
Code that constructs training examples and fits the five comparison classifiers.
training data manifest
Exact source reports, PDF hashes, report splits and annotation coverage.
Materialized training annotations
Explicit heading line groups and levels reviewed by the assistant.
later filter protocol
Records the same model hashes before the subsequent confidence-filter search.
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
A pretrained sparse vision-language model; only a subset of its expert parameters is active per token, although all weights are stored.
OvisOCR3
A compact visual language model from ATH-MaaS for document parsing and other OCR tasks. This row uses its Markdown task.
vLLM Metal
A community-maintained vLLM hardware plugin that runs supported models on Apple GPUs through MLX. It uses different kernels from NVIDIA Triton.
BF16
A 16-bit floating-point weight format. These are the original published weights, not a smaller quantized conversion.
LightOnOCR-3-0.8B
A document image-reading model with approximately 0.8 billion parameters. Its output includes text and page regions.
Grounding
Returning text together with the page regions it refers to. In these OCR runs, the response locates title blocks; a location alone does not establish a heading’s level.
LightOnOCR-3-4B
The four-billion-parameter document image-reading model used in this run.
Docling
PDF conversion software used here to detect text, layout and headings.
EvidenceLab
An evaluation-document application whose parsing pipeline adds hierarchy and contents-list processing to Docling.
docling-hierarchical-pdf
The post-processor used by EvidenceLab to infer hierarchy from PDF metadata or heading layout and font measurements.
MinerU
Document parsing software; this row uses its basic CPU parser, not the separate Pro image model.
ONNX Runtime
Software that executes a model saved in the ONNX format. The basic MinerU run uses it on the CPU.
PP-DocLayoutV3
Paddle’s model for locating and classifying page regions, such as a title, paragraph, table or formula.
BF16
A 16-bit floating-point format for model weights. This run uses the original weights rather than a quantized conversion.
Qwen3.5-4B
A pretrained language model with approximately four billion parameters. Here it reads lists of possible headings and assigns levels.
Xiaomi-OCR-0
The upstream 0.8B-parameter visual recognition model, loaded from its pinned Hugging Face revision.
PyMuPDF4LLM
A library that converts PDF text and layout into Markdown, including heading markers.
Marker
Document conversion software. This run uses its local models on the CPU and reads heading tags from the output.
PaddleOCR-VL-1.6
The upstream 0.9B-parameter visual recognition model, loaded from its pinned Hugging Face revision.
PP-DocLayoutV3
A document-layout detector that labels regions such as titles, text, tables and figures. Its block labels and the Markdown assembler help determine the emitted hierarchy.
PaddleX
Paddle’s pipeline framework. This run uses its native layout detector and Markdown assembly, not MiniCPM’s replacements.
MiniCPM-OCR 1.0
The upstream 1.3B-parameter visual recognition model, loaded from its pinned Hugging Face revision.
MiniCPM-OCR
OpenBMB’s document-recognition model and official parsing package. The package also performs layout detection and Markdown assembly.
DSpark
A smaller draft model proposes several tokens at once; the main model checks them. Accepted draft tokens can reduce the number of main-model decoding steps.
Ollama
The local model server used by this official deployment. This run executes its model layers on Metal.
Q8_0
An 8-bit GGUF weight format. It is a quantized model file, so this row is distinct from the earlier BF16 configuration.
RapidOCR
An OCR package that detects text in images and recognizes the characters.
Heron
Docling’s layout model, which identifies regions such as text, headings and tables.
MinerU-Popo
A model and supporting code for assigning levels to document titles. This benchmark uses an experimental MLX adaptation.
MinerU2.5-Pro-2605-1.2B
The 1.2-billion-parameter document image model tested through its direct two-step interface. It supplied title blocks but no levels in this run.

We scored eight selected pages per report. Page numbers are physical PDF pages, counting from the cover. Pages span front matter, chapters, subsections and annexes; this is not a random sample. The assistant-created reference labels have not been independently reviewed.

The original 2018 resilience report was excluded after document-specific exploratory work. Scanned documents are outside this experiment. None of these PDFs has outline bookmarks; some Qwen configurations do use available author-supplied structure tags.

What we verified: on the mid-term report's PDF page 26, “1. Introduction” is visually the main section and “1.1 Evaluation features” its subsection. The earlier MiniCPM assembler emits both as H3. It also promotes the ordinary paragraph “3. The MTE's key features are:” to a heading. Paddle's full pipeline reproduces these three outputs on that page.

In the earlier Xiaomi whole-page run, 65 of its 69 matched titles were H2. Those titles span reference levels H1-H5, so changing every level by one cannot fix the result. We have applied no offsets or rules fitted to these reports.

Xiaomi's upstream default formatter assigns H2 to paragraph titles. Executing that formatter on H1, H3 and numbered example titles returned H2 each time. On mid-term page 26, both Introduction and its Evaluation features subsection are H2. The upstream two-stage run still has 37 wrong-level matches; no WFP correction was applied.

OvisOCR3 sometimes transcribes a title without marking it as a heading. On Indonesia page 7, Executive summary, Introduction and Evaluation features appear as ordinary text. On targeting page 33, 2 Evaluation findings has no heading marker, although its subsections have H2-H4 markers. These are classification misses, not necessarily unreadable or absent text.

How to read the table
  • Timing: large models ran one at a time on a shared 48 GB M4 Pro. Other workloads were not controlled. Setup exclusions vary by configuration; each method records its timing scope.
  • Scope: Full-document parsers, including Docling OCR and EvidenceLab, read all 523 pages. Vision-to-text models read 32 audit pages. Qwen3.6 timing excludes candidate extraction; Qwen3.5 and Popo time only the hierarchy stage.
  • Measured versus estimated: a 32-page run is measured. Scaling a longer run’s average to 32 pages is estimated. Neither is a promise of individual-page latency.
  • Prose retention: the share of five-word sequences retained from native PDF blocks with at least 50 words. This does not measure reading order, table accuracy or meaning.
  • Cost: hardware, electricity, setup and review were not priced. Local execution is not zero-cost. Model licenses are separate from the repository’s MIT license.
  • Reproduction: frozen labels and predictions reproduce scores without downloading models. Full raw responses remain external. Commands and limits · Licenses.

Configuration-specific exceptions and training records are linked from each method’s details.

Sequential GPU reruns

Seven selected MLX configurations were rerun one at a time on the same four PDFs, 32 audit pages and 77 reference headings. Every rerun reproduced the original heading titles, pages and levels exactly, with no parse errors, timeouts or token-limit truncations. The main table now uses these new timings, marked “Latest sequential run”; this comparison preserves the original measurements.

Chandra and the two LightOn runs took 14–31% less processing time. Qwen results were mixed: visual-memory 27B improved 12.5%, while single-image 27B took 4.7% longer. Median system GPU utilization ranged from 92% to 100%, with the Metal GPU independently verified inside each inference process. These observations confirm GPU execution; they do not establish optimal kernel efficiency or isolate the effect of background load.

How these reruns were measured: protocol, settings and hardware

Execution and provenance: each configuration ran in a fresh process and output directory, with only one benchmark model loaded at a time. The runner checked the default MLX device and Metal availability before model loading. It retained model/package versions, source and input hashes, raw page responses, process wall time, GPU activity and virtual-memory counters. The main timing column accepts only error-free, untruncated reruns with the same page scope and exactly matching heading predictions; the historical source evidence remains unchanged.

Timing: all rates below use seconds per page. Earlier and rerun processing rates use the original runners' measurement boundaries, excluding model loading and upstream candidate extraction. Whole-process rates include interpreter imports, model loading, image preparation, generation and output writes; they still exclude previously prepared candidate extraction and downloads. OCR batch time is divided by the number of pages, so it measures average throughput rather than single-page latency. Smaller values are faster. This is one repeat per configuration, not a statistical estimate of typical performance.

Settings: Qwen models retain their pinned MLX 4-bit weights, greedy decoding, seed 42, non-thinking prompts and 4,096-token limit. Single-image runs use a 1,280-pixel image; visual-memory runs use a 1,792-pixel current image plus up to six earlier 1,280-pixel images. Chandra retains batch four and a 12,384-token limit. LightOn 4B uses batch two throughout and a 12,384-token limit; its historical run mixed five single-page checkpoints (12,288-token limit) with batching, so that comparison includes a batching and token-limit change. LightOn 0.8B remains one image at a time with an 8,192-token limit. No headings or levels are repaired after generation.

Hardware and limits: this Mac has an Apple M4 Pro with a 20-core GPU and 48 GiB unified memory. GPU inference is active, but other applications still share memory and GPU resources. In the initial rerun, loading the sparse Qwen model increased total system swap usage from approximately 15 GB to 20 GB. The reruns therefore must not be described as measurements on an idle or memory-pressure-free machine. Swap-counter differences below show actual activity during each run, rather than treating existing swap allocation as proof of ongoing paging. PDF rendering, tokenization and JSON handling also use the CPU. MLX's unified-memory and device documentation explains how CPU and GPU execution share memory; the recorded device selection and telemetry establish what happened in these runs.

Configuration

The exact parser, model and settings used for this measured run. Variants of the same model are separate configurations.

Use the information button beside a configuration to see its diagram, parameters, training or tuning, limitations, and links to code and original sources.

Time for 32 pages

Measured means the recorded processing time for the 32 audit pages.

Estimated means the recorded average time per page multiplied by 32. These methods were timed over a different page count, shown alongside their actual measured total. This is a linear projection, not a separate 32-page run or an exact time for the audit pages. Page complexity and fixed setup costs can change the result.

Unavailable means no processing time or page denominator was recorded. All times retain the original measurement scope; see each method for included and excluded stages.

Primary score: joint F0.5

The primary ranking score rewards a heading only when its title matches on the correct PDF page and its H level is exactly right. Higher is better.

Let C be correct title-and-level pairs, P all predicted headings and G reference headings. Joint F0.5 = 1.25C / (P + 0.25G). It emphasizes precision more than recall. Extra headings and wrong levels reduce the score; missing headings also count against it. Empty output scores zero.

The table is sorted by this score. There is no separate PASS/FAIL qualification gate.

Joint precision

The fraction of all emitted headings with the correct title, PDF page and exact H level: C / P. A wrong level, an absent level or an extra heading counts against precision.

For MinerU basic, 31 of 68 predictions have the correct heading and level: 45.6%. Matching 66 genuine titles is insufficient because 35 have the wrong level.

The count beside the percentage is correct heading-level pairs / all predictions. No predictions gives zero precision by this benchmark's convention.

Joint recall

The count and percentage of all 77 reference headings recovered on the correct page with the exact H level: C / G. This is joint recall, not the primary score.

Missing headings and wrong levels reduce this percentage. Extra predictions do not reduce it directly, which is why joint F0.5 is used for ranking. An absent level earns no joint credit.

Method / code

A summary of the actual execution path: inputs, model or parser, settings and processing scope. Select the method link to open its detailed diagram and code/source links.

The same model can produce different results with different inputs or settings. These results describe the recorded configurations, not every possible use of the underlying package.

Status

Whether the benchmark run completed. This table includes completed local configurations only.

Completed does not mean that the configuration is accurate or supplies every required output.

Headings recovered

The count and percentage of all 77 reference titles matched on the correct PDF page, regardless of level: M / G.

Matching normalizes title text, uses one-to-one assignment and requires at least 90% title similarity on the same page. It tolerates small text differences; it is not a character-perfect transcription test.

False headings

Predictions on audited pages that do not match a reference heading title on that page: P minus M. Lower is better.

A genuine heading with the wrong level is not included in this extra-heading count, but it does count as an error in joint F0.5. Counts cover the 32 audit pages, not every page parsed.

Native prose retention

The fraction of five-word sequences from longer native PDF text blocks retained in extracted text on the audit pages. Higher means more of this reference prose survived extraction.

This is a limited proxy, not a measure of reading order, table accuracy, semantic accuracy or downstream search quality. A dash means unavailable or not evaluated, not zero.

Time per page

Entries marked Latest sequential run use the newest completed sequential measurement whose heading titles, pages and levels exactly reproduce the original predictions. The comparison below retains the earlier measurements. Other entries retain their historical timing.

Total processing time divided by the number of pages actually processed. Durations use hours, minutes and seconds, with decimals for short runs. This is average throughput, not individual-page latency. Hierarchy-only runs without a recorded page denominator show an unavailable average and retain their total time; no denominator is invented.

Timings were recorded on a shared 48 GB Apple M4 Pro and are not a controlled speed benchmark. Qwen and Popo hierarchy times exclude upstream extraction. Exact inclusions and exclusions are described in each method's details.

These are local runs. Hardware, electricity, setup, review and licensing costs were not measured in dollars.

Vision + document context · local MLX

Qwen3.6-27B / MLX 4-bit / sampled visual memory

Qwen3.6-27B uses 4-bit MLX weights. Each call receives the current page, up to six earlier sampled images, native text, candidate titles and author PDF tags.

Exact run settings
Modelmlx-community/Qwen3.6-27B-4bit; revision c000ac2c2057
Page orderingAudit targets processed in ascending order within each report; memory resets between reports
RenderingPyMuPDF Matrix(2,2), nominal 144 dpi; target thumbnail ≤1792; memory thumbnails ≤1280 pixels
MemoryLatest predicted heading page at each of H1–H6; deduplicate pages, sort; at most six earlier sampled images
Generationenable_thinking=False; temperature=0; max_tokens=4096; seed=42
TimeoutSoft 600-second limit, checked between streamed chunks

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Learned classifiers · local CPU

OUR METHOD — confidence-filtered v2 (F0.5-selected)

OUR METHOD reuses three locally trained Extra Trees classifiers. A validation-selected 0.70 score cutoff rejects uncertain headings before sequence decoding. Correct heading-level pairs fall from 50 to 34; extras fall from 23 to two.

Exact run settings
Estimatorsklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier; scikit-learn 1.9.1; Python 3.12.3
Trees per classifiern_estimators=200
Tree limitsmax_depth=16; min_samples_leaf=2
Feature sampling / weightingmax_features=0.8; class_weight="balanced"
Reproducibility / parallelismrandom_state=42; n_jobs=4
Other estimator optionsLibrary defaults; no tree hyperparameter search was run
Join classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 100 features; 6,267 pairs; 200 trees; separate/join
Context classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 47 features; 6,736 groups; 200 trees; body/H1–H5
Relation classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 142 features; 867 heading pairs; 200 trees; shallower/same/deeper
Total deployed trees3 ×200 =600; join + context + relation
Decision filterbody_weight=1.0; min_heading_score=0.70; relation_weight=1.0
Selection objectiveMaximum validation joint F0.5 among candidates with heading precision ≥0.95; empty output fails
Grid36 settings: learned_groups/context_relations × body {1,2,4} × score {0,.5,.7,.85}; contextual relation {1,0}
MatchingSame physical page; normalized title similarity ≥0.90; exact H level; pooled counts before scoring

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B uses the original multi-image prompt with 4-bit weights. It restores up to six earlier sampled images alongside text, candidates and author tags.

Exact run settings

ArchitectureMoE 35B total / approximately 3B active; 40 text layers; width 2048; 256 routed experts, 8 selected per token

Interpretation

Removing visual history and shrinking the target image may lose typography clues. Correct title-and-level recall and false headings must be considered together. Only the original 32 sampled pages were scored.

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Whole-page vision-language document parsing

OvisOCR3 — upstream prompt and vLLM Metal

OvisOCR3 uses original 0.8B BF16 weights through vLLM Metal. The official document_markdown prompt and cleanup produce the scored Markdown.

Exact run settings
CheckpointATH-MaaS/OvisOCR3 @5b252386ba615bd464a5a26597560eaba87dae5c
Weights0.8B parameters; original BF16 weights; no quantization or WFP fine-tuning
Runtimevllm==0.34.0+cpu with vllm-metal==0.34.0; MLX backend on Apple M4 Pro GPU
Official-example differenceModel card uses vLLM 0.22.1 with gdn_prefill_backend=triton. Metal selects its own kernels; this is not a CUDA benchmark replication.
PromptPinned prompts/document_markdown.txt; official chat template; enable_thinking=False
Samplingtemperature=0; max_tokens=16384; seed=42; max_num_seqs=1; tensor_parallel_size=1
ImagesOne RGB image per call; minimum 448×448 and maximum 2880×2880 pixel area; current processor size API
Memorygpu_memory_utilization=0.8; native Metal attention kernels; upstream default context limit 262144
CleanupFilter image-tag blocks; upstream repeated-tail thresholds: minimum text 8000 characters, period 1–200, repeat span ≥100 characters and ≥5 repetitions
Timing418.19 seconds for 32 pages (13.07 seconds/page); 20.64 seconds model initialization separately
Completion32/32 pages; zero errors; zero length-limit stops; raw responses, tokens and finish reasons retained

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Learned classifiers · local CPU

OUR METHOD v2 + calibrated decoding (CPU)

The same three trained Extra Trees classifiers are reused. Multiplying the body-text score by two makes heading selection stricter; relationship weight stays 1.

Exact run settings
Estimatorsklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier; scikit-learn 1.9.1; Python 3.12.3
Trees per classifiern_estimators=200
Tree limitsmax_depth=16; min_samples_leaf=2
Feature sampling / weightingmax_features=0.8; class_weight="balanced"
Reproducibility / parallelismrandom_state=42; n_jobs=4
Other estimator optionsLibrary defaults; no tree hyperparameter search was run
Join classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 100 features; 6,267 pairs; 200 trees; separate/join
Context classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 47 features; 6,736 groups; 200 trees; body/H1–H5
Relation classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 142 features; 867 heading pairs; 200 trees; shallower/same/deeper
Total deployed trees3 ×200 =600; join + context + relation
Grid actually searchedbody_weight ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0}; relation_weight ∈ {1.0, 0.5, 0.0}; 9 combinations
Selected decodingbody_weight=2.0; relation_weight=1.0
Selection metric / tiesValidation exact group-and-level F1; first grid entry wins ties, with baseline settings ordered first
Model integritySame JSON model hashes as v2; no refitting or label changes

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Learned classifiers · local CPU

v2: context + relationships (selected)

Three 200-tree Extra Trees classifiers learn line joining, heading levels and relationships. Viterbi selects a level sequence using document context and relationship weight 1.

Exact run settings
Estimatorsklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier; scikit-learn 1.9.1; Python 3.12.3
Trees per classifiern_estimators=200
Tree limitsmax_depth=16; min_samples_leaf=2
Feature sampling / weightingmax_features=0.8; class_weight="balanced"
Reproducibility / parallelismrandom_state=42; n_jobs=4
Other estimator optionsLibrary defaults; no tree hyperparameter search was run
Join classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 100 features; 6,267 pairs; 200 trees; separate/join
Context classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 47 features; 6,736 groups; 200 trees; body/H1–H5
Relation classifierExtraTreesClassifier: 142 features; 867 heading pairs; 200 trees; shallower/same/deeper
Total deployed trees3 ×200 =600; join + context + relation
Decodingbody_weight=1.0; relation_weight=1.0; Viterbi over retained H1–H5 candidates
Artifacts / fitting23.2 MiB combined JSON; ≈2.09 s summed classifier fitting, excluding extraction/export/validation

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Learned classifiers · local CPU

v2: learned grouping

Two 200-tree Extra Trees classifiers learn line joining and heading levels. This variant uses 100 join features and 43 group features, without document context.

Exact run settings
Estimatorsklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier; scikit-learn 1.9.1; Python 3.12.3
Trees per classifiern_estimators=200
Tree limitsmax_depth=16; min_samples_leaf=2
Feature sampling / weightingmax_features=0.8; class_weight="balanced"
Reproducibility / parallelismrandom_state=42; n_jobs=4
Other estimator optionsLibrary defaults; no tree hyperparameter search was run
Join classifier100 features; 6,267 labeled adjacent-line pairs; classes 0=separate, 1=join
Group classifier43 features; 6,736 examples; classes body/H1–H5
Total deployed trees2 ×200 =400
Artifact sizes / fitjoin.json 1,958,200 bytes / ≈0.816 s; group.json 17,519,049 bytes / ≈0.995 s

11—H3 — The CSP for 2021–2025 has facilitated WFP’s continued strategic positioning in Indonesia and supported the Government in its efforts to achieve its SDG targets. The CSP has contributed to WFP’s increased strategic engagement in an array of humanitarian and development sectors, particularly with regard to strengthening national systems for humanitarian response and food security. The CSP structure has allowed operational flexibility and responsiveness to emerging opportunities and changes in circumstances; however, while CSP activities are aligned with the priorities of government partners, they do not address some issues affecting women, older people, persons with disabilities, people living in remote areas, and children – groups identified in the common country analysis as those most at risk of being left behind. Supervised Extra Trees / CPU / assistant labels

OUR METHOD v1 uses one 200-tree Extra Trees classifier trained on 16 WFP reports. It labels PDF text lines, then joins adjacent same-level lines within each block.

Exact run settings
Estimatorsklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier; scikit-learn 1.9.1; Python 3.12.3
Trees per classifiern_estimators=200
Tree limitsmax_depth=16; min_samples_leaf=2
Feature sampling / weightingmax_features=0.8; class_weight="balanced"
Reproducibility / parallelismrandom_state=42; n_jobs=4
Other estimator optionsLibrary defaults; no tree hyperparameter search was run
Training set154 heading groups / 16 WFP reports
Alternative estimatorStandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C=1, class_weight="balanced", max_iter=3000, random_state=42)
Selected artifact200-tree JSON model, 9.97 MiB; recorded fit time ≈0.455 s, excluding preparation

Two-stage OCR · CPU layout and Metal recognition

Xiaomi-OCR-0 — upstream two-stage pipeline, Metal

Xiaomi’s upstream two-stage pipeline uses native PaddleX layout on CPU and BF16 recognition through vLLM Metal. Its default formatter assigns paragraph titles H2.

Exact run settings
Weightsxiaomi-research/Xiaomi-OCR-0, original BF16; revision bbd8cf8d21f256b3644b44cb860f3a7cecb93c30
Upstream codeSeerRay-Lab/Xiaomi-OCR-0, revision 4abc240285b69a2965cf64762101ddb4ab35f32d
LayoutPaddleX 3.7.2 / PaddlePaddle 3.3.1; native PP-DocLayoutV3; CPU; threshold=0.25
Recognition runtimevLLM 0.34.0 with vllm-metal 0.34.0; original BF16; one concurrent sequence; seed=42; GPU memory fraction=0.8
Decodingtemperature=0; top_p=0.8; presence_penalty=0; repetition_penalty=1; max_tokens=16384; timeout=600 seconds
Repetition retryEnabled; retry presence penalty=1.5; same-character run=128; minimum repeats=8; minimum repeated characters=512; ratio=0.5; maximum unit=256 characters
AssemblyDefault MergeOptions(title_profile="v2"); no number-based title profile or hierarchy repair
ConcurrencyOne OCR model at a time; one page and one upstream worker at a time

Qwen3.5-4B / union candidates

Qwen3.5-4B, quantized to 4 bits, assigns levels to the combined Docling and PyMuPDF4LLM candidate list. It receives text and page numbers only.

Exact run settings
Modelmlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit; revision 32f3e8ecf654 (full pin in configs/models.json)
InputOne full-document text candidate list; num_images=0; enable_thinking=False
Generationtemperature=0; max_tokens=4096; prefill_step_size=256; MLX seed=42
Candidate sourceDocling + PyMuPDF4LLM
Output contractExact input-ID key set; integer level 1–20 or null; invalid response produces null levels for that document
TuningFixed prompt and pretrained quantized weights; no fine-tuning or recorded prompt search

Whole-page vision-language OCR

Xiaomi-OCR-0 — MLX whole page

Xiaomi-OCR-0 reads whole-page images through MLX using e2e_img2md. Its generated Markdown supplies the heading levels.

Exact run settings
Modelxiaomi-research/Xiaomi-OCR-0; revision bbd8cf8d21f256b3644b44cb860f3a7cecb93c30
Model size / weights0.8B parameters; original BF16 weights, no weight quantization or fine-tuning
RuntimeMLX 0.32.4; mlx-vlm 0.8.0; Transformers 5.23.0; Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB unified memory
Input32 fixed physical PDF pages; PyMuPDF render at 200 DPI; pixels only
Decodingtemperature=0; seed=42; enable_thinking=False
ConcurrencyOne model and one page at a time; region recognition sequential; Metal kernels internally parallel
LimitsSoft 600-second timeout per recognition request, checked between streamed chunks
TimingIncludes rendering, CPU layout when used, recognition and assembly; model loading recorded separately
Output budget16,384 tokens per whole page
PromptExact upstream evaluation_pipeline/e2e_img2md.py whole-page Markdown instruction; recorded in runner

Packagepymupdf4llm==2.1
Callto_markdown(pdf, page_chunks=True, use_ocr=False)
Heading parserStart-of-line #{1,6}, followed by whitespace and nonempty text
Tuning / promptNo benchmark fitting, prompt or manual font-threshold override; other options use package defaults

Text-only LLM refinement · local MLX

Qwen3.5-4B / MinerU candidates

Qwen3.5-4B, quantized to 4 bits, assigns levels to MinerU basic candidates. It receives text and page numbers only.

Exact run settings
Modelmlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit; revision 32f3e8ecf654 (full pin in configs/models.json)
InputOne full-document text candidate list; num_images=0; enable_thinking=False
Generationtemperature=0; max_tokens=4096; prefill_step_size=256; MLX seed=42
Candidate sourceMinerU basic
Output contractExact input-ID key set; integer level 1–20 or null; invalid response produces null levels for that document
TuningFixed prompt and pretrained quantized weights; no fine-tuning or recorded prompt search

Official PaddleOCR Apple Silicon pipeline

PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 — official Apple Silicon pipeline

PaddleOCR 3.7.0 runs the complete v1.6 pipeline: native PaddleX layout on CPU, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 on Metal, then Paddle’s Markdown assembler.

Exact run settings
Pipelinepaddleocr==3.7.0; paddlex==3.7.2; paddlepaddle==3.3.1; pipeline_version=v1.6
WeightsPaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 @132c45f52c0a26ed5a6b2f6bd8e3985794cc27dd; original BF16
HardwareApple M4 Pro; 48 GB unified memory; Paddle layout on CPU, MLX recognition on Metal
ConcurrencyOne model, one page and one recognition request at a time; use_queues=False; vl_rec_max_concurrency=1
LayoutPP-DocLayoutV3 native Paddle weights; threshold=0.3; native v1.6 merging defaults
Recognitiontemperature=0; upstream per-region output budget and task prompts
Other pipeline optionsv1.6 defaults: chart recognition=False, seal recognition=False, document preprocessing=False; merge_layout_blocks=True
Image bounds limitationPaddle’s mlx-vlm client warns that min_pixels and max_pixels are not supported by this backend. The model processor uses its own bounds.
Timing291.97 seconds for 32 pages (9.12 seconds/page). Includes rendering, layout, recognition, assembly and JSON saving. CPU pipeline initialization: 1.52 seconds separately. Recognition model was preloaded.
Request telemetryNo page errors. Per-request finish reasons and token-limit counts are not exposed by this pipeline, so they are not reported as zero.

Layout detection plus regional vision-language OCR

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 — MLX + CPU layout

PP-DocLayoutV3 finds crops on CPU. MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 reads them through MLX; MiniCPM SDK 1.0.5 assembles Markdown.

Exact run settings
Modelopenbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0; revision 883ca368d17335b9ce5aa6fef4d000ef0684fcaa
Model size / weights1.3B parameters; original BF16 weights, no weight quantization or fine-tuning
RuntimeMLX 0.32.4; mlx-vlm 0.8.0; Transformers 5.23.0; Apple M4 Pro, 48 GB unified memory
Input32 fixed physical PDF pages; PyMuPDF render at 200 DPI; pixels only
Decodingtemperature=0; seed=42; enable_thinking=False
ConcurrencyOne model and one page at a time; region recognition sequential; Metal kernels internally parallel
LimitsSoft 600-second timeout per recognition request, checked between streamed chunks
TimingIncludes rendering, CPU layout when used, recognition and assembly; model loading recorded separately

Layout settingsCPU; torch.set_num_threads(4); threshold=0.3; nms=True; chart and seal recognition enabled; image-block OCR disabled
SDKminicpm-ocr==1.0.5; direct detector/crop/assemble_markdown components
Output budgetsUpstream class recipes: titles 512; body text 4096; tables 8192; display formulas 2048; charts 4096; seals 256 tokens
HierarchySDK title_style=numbered; no offset correction or WFP-specific rules

Interpretation

This is a portable MLX recognition and CPU layout adaptation. It is not the vendor’s CUDA deployment, and its speed cannot be compared directly with the NVIDIA field chart.

Benchmark code ↗Official model and model card ↗Upstream implementation and documentation ↗Download pins ↗Protocol and reproduction commands ↗Measured predictions and page telemetry ↗PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 paper ↗

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Official MiniCPM package with quantized recognition and speculative decoding

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 — official package, Ollama Q8 + DSpark

MiniCPM-OCR 1.0.5 handles orientation, native PaddleX layout and Markdown assembly. Ollama runs the official Q8 model with DSpark speculative decoding on Metal.

Exact run settings
Packageminicpm-ocr==1.0.5; paddlepaddle==3.3.1; paddleocr==3.7.0; paddlex==3.7.2
Main and vision filesMiniCPM-OCR-1_0-Q8_0.gguf and mmproj-model-f16-4x.gguf; openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0-gguf @0133ad8db635210441a55dcf421e25bfb9915142
Draft filedspark-MiniCPM-OCR-1_0-Q8_0.gguf; openbmb/MiniCPM-OCR-1.0-DSpark-gguf @cab493a5a26516a1c4c6e07c73b4470ff854a898
Weight verificationThe runner verifies that Ollama’s registered main, projector and draft blob hashes match the pinned official files.
RuntimeOllama 0.40.17; llama.cpp engine on Apple M4 Pro Metal; 48 GB unified memory
Samplingtemperature=0; top_p=0.001; top_k=1; repeat_penalty=1; Ollama num_ctx=8192; draft_num_predict=15
ConcurrencyOne model configuration and one recognition request at a time. SDK queue_mode=concurrent can group regions across pages; max_workers=1 and page_workers=1; layout/recognition overlap=False.
Layout and orientationNative PP-DocLayoutV3, threshold=0.3, nms=True; SDK orientation models downloaded and warmed before the scored run
Output budgetsSDK class defaults: paragraph/doc titles 512; body text 4096; table 8192; display formula 2048; chart 4096; seal 256
Timing465.87 seconds measured for 32 pages (14.56 seconds/page). Includes rendering and the complete CPU pipeline initialization. Ollama weights were loaded by the cover smoke test.
ResultJoint F0.5 22.2%; 16/77 correct title-level pairs; 3 extra predictions; heading metrics unchanged from the earlier BF16 MLX adaptation.

Shared methods and scoring · Run code · Full run record

Full-page OCR · CPU

Docling — full-page RapidOCR + heading hierarchy

Docling 2.151.1 reads every page image with RapidOCR, using PP-OCRv5 mobile detection and Latin-script recognition. Heron detects layout, then HeadingHierarchyModel assigns heading levels.

Exact run settings
Packagesdocling==2.151.1; docling-core==2.108.0; rapidocr==3.10.0; onnxruntime==1.32.0; torch==2.15.0; pymupdf==2.1
OCRmode=FULL_PAGE; lang=[latin]; backend=onnxruntime; scale=3.0 (216 dpi); model_size=small; text_score=0.5; detect_orientation=False
Recognition modelsch_PP-OCRv5_det_mobile.onnx; latin_PP-OCRv5_rec_mobile.onnx; ch_ppocr_mobile_v2.0_cls_mobile.onnx
DeviceCPU; num_threads=8
Conversiondo_ocr=True; do_table_structure=False; generate_parsed_pages=True
HierarchyHeadingHierarchyOptions(enabled=True); remaining settings use defaults
Scored outputNative SectionHeaderItem text, level and first provenance page
TimingFull-PDF conversion plus hierarchy; initialization recorded separately
Observed time9 min 23 sec for 523 pages; 4.12 sec initialization excluded; 1.08 sec/page average
Model pinsHeron revision 8f39ad3c0b4c58e9c2d2c84a38465abf757272d8; OCR weight hashes in configs/docling-ocr-models.json
